question: Which of the following events marks the high-water mark of French territorial and political influence in the Deccan, prior to the English counter-offensive led by Robert Clive?
options: The signing of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748.
The installation of Salabat Jung as Nizam of Hyderabad and the stationing of Bussy's army at Aurangabad, accompanied by the acquisition of the Northern Circars.
The capture of Calcutta by Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah with French naval assistance.
The defeat of the British navy at the Battle of Wandiwash in 1760.
explanation: The peak of French influence was achieved between 1751 and 1753 under Dupleix and Bussy. After Muzaffar Jung's death, Bussy installed Salabat Jung as the Nizam of Hyderabad. Salabat Jung remained highly dependent on Bussy's army (stationed at Hyderabad/Aurangabad) and ceded the Northern Circars (comprising the coastal revenue-rich districts of Ellore, Chicacole, Rajahmundry, and Condapalli) to the French. This gave the French a massive territorial empire and immense political leverage, which was later lost due to Clive's capture of Arcot and subsequent developments.
